readout_other: motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude; short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI); intracortical facilitation (ICF); resting motor threshold (RMT); SI1mV
direction_notes: In the placebo condition, tbTUS increased MEP amplitude relative to pre-tbTUS baseline for up to 60 min post-stimulation; this facilitatory effect was reduced/eliminated by carbamazepine, nimodipine, and dextromethorphan, and by lorazepam at 30 and 60 (but not 5) minutes post-tbTUS.
safety_notes: The same subject also reported mild itchiness for NDP, CBZ and DXT, particularly over the scalp area where the TUS transducer was placed. There were no unexpected side effects when administering TUS and drugs together.

timing.protocol_description: As with Zeng et al. [7], an 80s sonication with tone burst duration of 20 ms, 5Hz PRF, 10% duty cycle and 20W intensity was delivered. Sonication depth was set to 30 mm to approximate the scalp-to-cortex distance of the M1. One tbTUS delivery occurred per visit, after a 2.5 h drug/placebo wait period, at each of five study visits.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Sixteen right-handed healthy adult subjects (4 females) participated in the study, which consisted of five separate visits. Two male subjects dropped out during or after the first visit due to disregarding researcher instructions. The remaining 14 subjects had a mean age ±SD of 30.4 ± 6.3 (range 23–41) years.

flags.reason: 16 subjects enrolled; 2 dropped out after visit 1 and are excluded from most analyses (14 analysed for most drugs, 13 for LRZ/DXT). n_subjects reported here is the enrolled total.

Paper calls this a 'tone burst duration' of 20 ms within an 80 s train; consistent with duty cycle (10%) / PRF (5 Hz) = 20 ms, so no arithmetic conflict, but confirming burst-rule resolution here for transparency.
Study tested drug x tbTUS only; no sham/control tbTUS condition was included (explicitly noted as a limitation).
